newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-VOGTS DENIES HE WANTS PLAYOFF ON WORLD CUP ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VOGTS DENIES HE WANTS PLAYOFF ON WORLD CUP ROW.

text.p: Germany coach Berti Vogts on Thursday denied he had challenged England to a match to decide who bids for the 2006 World Cup finals but said if England withdrew their bid Germany would be happy to play them.
"If England withdraw their bid in the competition to host the World Cup then we would love to play them in a friendly," Vogts said.
The German soccer federation (DFB) said Vogts had never suggested the arch rivals take their row over the 2006 finals on to the pitch, as reported by the British Mirror tabloid on Thursday.

The newspaper quoted Vogts as saying the row had caused so much bad blood that the only way to clear the air was to play a friendly match for the right to make Europe's bid and said many English soccer experts backed the idea.
Just last week, Vogts called on English soccer officials to withdraw their bid for the 2006 World Cup finals because they did not have the support of the whole of Europe.
Speaking after former World Cup coach and captain Franz Beckenbauer attacked the English Football Association (F.A.), Vogts said the English would pull out if they had any character.
The Germans launched their cup campaign in 1993 under the impression that the English F.A. would support them as Europe's leading candidate.

But the English body decided to run a rival bid after last year's successful staging of the European championship finals. Beckenbauer said the English F.A. had left Germany in the lurch by launching their own bid.

FIFA does not decide until the year 2000 which country will host the finals. Rival bids are also expected from South America and Africa. The Germans are worried that Europe will miss out if they have two bids.
